name: Un-Scripted Theater Company®
note: Wikipedia uses past tense (2002 to 2020) but un-scripted.com is live, now titled SF Improv Theater, still at 533 Sutter St.

facts.text: An improvised theater company founded in 2002.
Specializes in narrative and genre-based single-story improvised theater.
Built in 1908 as Brown's Opera House, a vaudeville house, by Edmund Joseph Brown.
Renamed the 16th Street Theater in the 1930s and El Teatro Victoria in the 1950s, showing Spanish-language movies.
Described as the oldest operating theatre in San Francisco.

name: Video Wave
note: Matched to Video Wave of Noe Valley, 4027 24th St, near the given lat/lng.

facts.text: A video rental store that moved along 24th Street with customers helping fund and carry out the move.
Opened in 1910 as the Elite Theatre, renamed Rex Theatre in 1919 and Plaza Theatre by 1932.
Reopened as the Vogue Theatre on July 1, 1938.

name: War Memorial Veterans Building Herbst Theatre

facts.text: Site of the signing of the United Nations Charter on June 26, 1945.
Features Frank Brangwyn murals originally painted for the 1915 Panama-Pacific International Exposition.
Designed by architect G. Albert Lansburgh.
Opened as the Loews Warfield, a vaudeville theater, and later became the Fox Warfield.

name: Westside Art House
note: Matched to Westside Art House, 540 Balboa St, near the given lat/lng; Yelp lists it updated Jan 2026 as a dance and movement studio.

facts.text: Opened in 2011 as part dance studio, part art gallery and part community center.
Started by Marisa Gregory, a trained yoga instructor.

name: Wildlife Theater
note: Matched to the Wells Fargo Wildlife Theatre at San Francisco Zoo (lat/lng is at the zoo).

facts.text: Hosts summer wildlife shows on conservation and history, with free-flying birds of prey and animal ambassadors.
Sits across from the Dentzel Carousel, next to Flamingo Lake.

name: Young Performers Theatre
note: Located at Fort Mason Center, matching the given lat/lng.

facts.text: A nonprofit children's theatre founded by Matilda Kunin in 1983 in memory of her son Anthony.
Offers introductory acting classes to children as young as three.
A small open space with a view over Noe Valley and beyond.

name: Adam Rodgers Park
note: City page names it Adam Rogers Park (Ingalls and Oakdale, Bayview).

name: Bayview Gateway
note: Matched to Bayview Gateway Park (Port of SF) at Cargo Way and 3rd Street; given lat/lng is roughly 700 m north, so location is approximate.

facts.text: A Port of San Francisco park with a skateboarding area with raised platforms, picnic tables and benches.
An active cargo rail line runs across the park, and Fire Department Station 25 is in it.

name: Bayview Playground
note: City page names it Bayview K.C. Jones Playground (3rd and Armstrong).

facts.text: Officially named Bayview/K.C. Jones Playground in 2003, after the basketball player who grew up nearby.
Reopened in January 2022 after a $6 million renovation with a new play area, ballfield and fitness equipment.
